facts.statement: The genus name Cryptarcus means “hidden arch”.
Cryptarcus is known from the Dinosaur Park Formation and dates to the middle Campanian of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: found in the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, dating to the middle Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The type species, Cryptarcus russelli, was originally described as Chasmosaurus russelli by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1940.
facts.quote: It was first named in 1940 by Charles Mortram Sternberg as a species of the genus Chasmosaurus and given the name Chasmosaurus russelli.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of most of an articulated skull, though the front snout, lower jaws, right half of the frill, and parts of the left face were missing and later reconstructed in plaster.
facts.quote: Most of the skull was preserved and fully articulated, but the front of the snout, the lower jaws, the right half of the frill, and various portions of the left side of the face were missing and were reconstructed with plaster

facts.statement: The median embayment angle of Cryptarcus frills ranges between 89° and 128°, a metric used to separate it from Chasmosaurus belli.
facts.quote: C. russelli had embayments formed by left and right posterior parietal bars meeting at angle between 89° and 128°, whereas those of C. belli met an angle between 136° and 180°.

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether the specimens previously referred to Chasmosaurus russelli represent a separate genus, with Nick Longrich proposing Mojoceratops perifania in 2010, a view largely rejected by other scientists.
facts.quote: In 2010 Nick Longrich argued many of the specimens referred to C. russelli actually represented a new genus and species, Mojoceratops perifania, but this was rejected by most other researchers.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Cryptarcus measures about 94 cm in length.
facts.quote: The holotype skull of Cryptarcus is around 94 cm long, while the rest of the skeleton remains unknown.

facts.statement: The parietosquamosal frill of Cryptarcus is about 120 % as long as the rest of the skull.
facts.quote: The parietosquamosal frill measures around 120% of the length of the rest of the skull.

facts.statement: Cryptarcus had a short, broad‑based nasal horn positioned over the back of the naris.
facts.quote: Located about the naris was a short and broad-based nasal horn.

facts.statement: The postorbital horns are preserved only as small stumps in the holotype, possibly pathological, but may have been long in life.
facts.quote: Though preserved as small stumps in the holotype (which may be pathological), they may have been quite long in life.

facts.statement: Cryptarcus possesses a prominent rugosity on the palpebral bone in front of each eye.
facts.quote: Underneath these horns, a bone in front of the eye known as the palpebral bears a prominent rugosity unique to Cryptarcus.

facts.statement: The frontoparietal fontanelle in the holotype is especially wide and has a unique bone bridge between the postorbital bones, likely due to old age.
facts.quote: This is a typical feature of ceratopsids, but is especially wide in the holotype of Cryptarcus, and possesses a unique bridge of bone between the postorbital bones on either side, possibly due to the old age of the individual rather than distinguishing the species.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Cryptarcus in an unresolved polytomy, sometimes closer to Pentaceratops and other times closer to Chasmosaurus, depending on the methodological iteration.
facts.quote: Iterations 3 and 5 (k = 3) recovered Cryptarcus in an unresolved polytomy with Agujaceratops spp., more closely related to Pentaceratops than Chasmosaurus, while Iterations 4 and 6 (k = 12) recovered it closer to Chasmosaurus than Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: Features once thought to unite Cryptarcus with Chasmosaurus, such as a low facial profile and thin parietal strut, are also found in other chasmosaurines and may be affected by taphonomic distortion.
facts.quote: Anatomical features that were believed to unite Cryptarcus with Chasmosaurus (low facial profile, rear maxilla hidden below jugal, thin parietal strut) can also be seen among other chasmosaurines and can be subject to taphonomic distortion.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis of only the holotype produced three consensus topologies, placing it variously closer to Chasmosaurus, closer to Pentaceratops, or unresolved.
The authors found no phylogenetic support for an anagenetic sequence from Cryptarcus russelli through Pentaceratops to Terminocavus as previously hypothesized.
